_comment: #548: a public address is moved onto the filtered NIC, and every guard
that makes the move safe or honest is falsified here.
The migration itself is falsified by lifecycle-tells-the-truth.json,
which owned #498's half of the same branch before it: releasing the
address from the routed NIC is what unblocks the uplink write that used
to fail with `file exists`, so one mutation answers for both.

mutations.label: networkd is not told to let go of eth0 before the re-plug, so the new link is matched and written in the window where the driver reads n/a and writes first (#742)

if running && routedDeviceCarriesNothing(after) {

mutations.replace:
if running && routedDeviceCarriesNothing(after) && false {
		if _, err := d.unmanageGuestInterface(ctx, machine, device); err != nil {

mutations.label: the drop-in is written and networkd never told to read it, so the file is one nobody has looked at and networkd goes on writing eth0 (#742)
the driver goes on before networkd reports the link unmanaged: an effect is waited for instead of the state the driver provoked (#742)
the boot after a cold migration does not tell networkd to let go, and the stale launch config keeps laying the migrated address at every boot (#742)

mutations.label: a cold migration is reconciled like a hot one, reading and writing the routed interface of a stopped machine (#742)
a guest with no networkd is written a drop-in beside a unit it does not have, and the shell inside it builds a directory from an empty name (#742)
the migration reconfigures an instance without asking whether the emulator created it
the address is taken off the machine before anyone asks whether the network it is moving to is ours
a routed NIC that carries nothing is reported as an escape again, so every migrated machine fails its firewall apply
the hot attach stops replaying the addresses, so the interface that just arrived never takes the published address
mutations.find:
err := r.attach(ctx, res, att)
	r.ReplayAddresses(ctx, res)

mutations.label: the driver goes back to answering one address, the first of the lowest-named interface
a restored value that is not an address is published to a client anyway
a restarted machine is left waiting for a lease nobody offers, so it comes back with neither its private address nor its routes
the boot's own record is never re-read, so it stays older than the machine by the addresses the replay installed
a runtime with nothing to say overwrites the record anyway, erasing what an earlier read had learned
